caption:
Cloudflare stopped treating every AI crawler like one problem. On July 1, 2026, Jin-Hee Lee and Bryan Becker said all customers, including Free, can manage AI traffic in three buckets: Search (index for later answers), Agent (real-time fetch for a human), and Training (content absorbed into models). Help Net Security summarized the same shift on July 2.

That matters because multipurpose crawlers inherit every policy you set. If you block Training, Cloudflare says bots that combine Search and Training, including Googlebot, Applebot, and BingBot, follow the strictest rule. Starting September 15, 2026, new domains will block Training and Agent on pages that show ads while keeping Search allowed. You can opt out in Security settings before that date.

robots.txt still signals preference, not a guarantee. Cloudflare's own AI Crawl Control docs track violations, and the December 2024 AI Audit update can translate robots.txt AI rules into WAF enforcement. Preference without edge enforcement is visibility, not control.

Inventory which crawlers you allow for search referrals, which agents may fetch on behalf of users, and which training crawlers you want gone. Then align managed robots.txt, crawler actions, and WAF rules before the September defaults reshape traffic you already monetize.

Will you opt out or tune those defaults before September 15?

Follow for AI security breakdowns without the fake panic.

narration.text: Cloudflare just split AI crawlers into Search, Agent, and Training so you are not stuck with one block-everything switch.
That sounds granular until you realize multipurpose bots inherit every policy, so blocking training can block search crawlers you still want.
On September fifteenth, new domains will block Training and Agent on ad pages by default, and you can opt out in Security settings before then.
robots.txt only states preference. Pair managed directives with WAF enforcement once you know which function each bot performs.
